---
title: "Dot Product — How Much Two Directions Agree"
description: "An original mathematical walkthrough with one running example, concrete numbers and a proof."
---

## Ask a simple question

How can we tell whether two arrows point mostly in the same direction or at right angles?

## Build the intuition

The dot product adds pairwise component products. A zero dot product in Euclidean space means the vectors are perpendicular.

## Write the mathematical relationship

$$
\mathbf u\cdot\mathbf v=u_1v_1+u_2v_2
$$

**Every symbol explained:** u and v are vectors; u₁,u₂ and v₁,v₂ are their horizontal and vertical components; the dot represents the dot product, not a new kind of multiplication yielding a vector.

**Substitute real numbers:** For u=(3,1) and v=(1,−3), the dot product is 3×1+1×(−3)=3−3=0. These arrows are perpendicular.

## Why the relationship is true

Geometrically the same value equals |u||v|cos θ, so zero corresponds to cos θ=0 when both vectors are nonzero: the angle is 90°.

## Where the shortcut stops working

A zero vector has dot product zero with every vector but has no unique direction; be precise when interpreting angles.

## Your turn

Test u=(2,0) and v=(3,4). Does a positive dot product prove the two arrows are parallel?

**Source structure:** Ivan Savov, *No Bullshit Guide to Linear Algebra*, second edition, Intro to linear algebra, §2.2 and geometric vector operations. This is an independently written explanation based on the uploaded **extended preview**, not a transcription of the commercial full book.
